title: JWST observations of the Ring Nebula (NGC 6720): III. A dusty disk around its Central Star

evidence.locator: Abstract: the central star is surrounded by a dust cloud with a size of about 2600 au, of small amorphous silicate grains (radius about 0.01 µm) with a total mass of 1.9e-6 Earth masses. Sect. IV.1: the best-fit DUSTY model is a shell with an inner radius of 10.5 au and a density power-law exponent p of about -0.8, density increasing outwards with radius; the modelling is one-dimensional because there is no direct information about the cloud's morphology, although the authors say it is likely disk-like. Table 4: inner radius 0.013 arcsec, 10.5 au; outer radius 1.66 arcsec, 1310 au; exponent n = -0.8 for a density going as r^-n; optical depth at 0.55 µm 1.3e-8; dust mass 1.86e-6 Earth masses.
